title: chinese ai firm moonshot explore dual hong kong shanghai ipos scmp reports 2026 09 10
text:
Sept 10 (Reuters) - Beijing-based AI startup Moonshot is considering dual listings in Hong Kong and Shanghai to boost fundraising and exposure, the South China ​Morning Post reported on Thursday, citing two people familiar with ‌the matter.
The developer of the Kimi large language model has discussed plans for a Hong Kong IPO with its financial backers and has also floated the ​possibility of a subsequent mainland listing, according to one of ​the people who spoke to SCMP.
Moonshot is likely to ⁠target the Shanghai Stock Exchange's STAR Market and could soon begin ​talks with the bourse, the report said.
The exchange's STAR Market refers to ​the Shanghai Stock Exchange Science and Technology Innovation Board, which has recently attracted other Chinese technology companies including Unitree Robotics.
Exploration of a mainland listing may reflect weaker ​performance among Hong Kong-listed AI stocks and a crowded IPO pipeline ​in the city, the newspaper reported, citing its sources.
Moonshot could not immediately be reached ‌for ⁠comment.
Reuters reported last week that Moonshot had confidentially filed for a Hong Kong IPO, citing three people with knowledge of the plans, with one saying it is aiming to raise $3 billion through the Hong Kong ​listing.
A listing by ​Moonshot would add ⁠to a wave of AI-related fundraising globally. Anthropic, the developer of Claude, is preparing an offering by ​October. Among Chinese firms, Z.AI, formerly known as Zhipu, ​and MiniMax ⁠listed in Hong Kong this year.
Moonshot's latest model, the Kimi K3, launched in July, has received positive reviews and strong demand. Sources told ⁠Reuters earlier ​the startup is in talks with ​Microsoft (MSFT.O)
